analyst_summary: June 10, 2026 morning opens at Vibe 3 — unchanged from June 9 close, firming slightly on the May CPI in-line result. The morning's defining event is the CPI print: 4.2% YoY in-line with consensus, highest since April 2023, core 2.9% in-line, monthly 0.2% below the 0.3% estimate. The Iran energy shock is fully legible in the data — gasoline +40.5% YoY, energy +23.5% YoY — but the in-line result removes the acute upside-surprise risk that dominated pre-FOMC anxiety. Shelter decelerated sharply (+0.3% MoM vs. +0.6% April) and is the single structural positive. The primary geopolitical structure is unchanged: MOU amendment counter-demand advances to Day 6 with no new Iranian response in the overnight cycle — six consecutive cycle days without a recovery catalyst since the Sunday June 7 window's passage. The three structural pillars sustaining Vibe 3 above 2 remain intact — Iran comms resolved Day 7 (channel integrity confirmed), Beirut-suburbs truce Day 8 clean (longest operative hold of the Lebanon track), and Brent ~$94 continuing easing (delay-not-collapse territory, no rejection risk premium). Today's primary action items: (1) House DHS/ICE reconciliation floor vote window Day 2 is live — Speaker Johnson's Tuesday-through-Thursday operative window runs through June 11; Freedom Caucus anti-weaponization dynamics remain the primary legislative risk; the in-line CPI removes the economic-data bandwidth competition from today's floor window; (2) FIFA Global Opening T-1 — the NIFC-FIFA co-response window is Live Day 3; today is the last 24-hour window before dual-mandate emergency operations become simultaneously active through July 6; Seattle CCTV activated on credible threats; 'Let's Play SEA 26' opens tomorrow at Seattle Center; (3) Warsh Day 27 silent, FOMC T-6 — the inaugural meeting is six days out; the in-line CPI print gives Warsh hawkish-pause framing space without forcing an immediate rate signal. Peru final certified result expected today–tomorrow; Sanchez 50.10% lead with international ballots outstanding. CIDRAP measles slowing signal advances to Day 3 — strongest deceleration confirmation to date. This morning's highest-priority watch items: any Iranian formal response to amendment counter-demand (primary Vibe catalyst); House DHS/ICE vote outcome this week; Brent direction post-CPI; Peru certified result announcement; NIFC overnight ignition report; FIFA pre-opening security posture.
